Glacier retreat in the eastern range

The eastern range has been surveyed every summer since the first aerial photographs were taken, and the record is long enough that the retreat can be separated from year-to-year variation in snowfall.

Between the two surveys the terminus moved back by roughly two kilometres, and the lower tongue thinned by an amount that the mass-balance stakes place between fifty and seventy metres.

The lake that formed at the terminus after 1998 now covers most of the former ice margin, and its depth has been sounded twice, most recently during the survey of 2021.

Downstream users draw on the summer melt, and the modelling suggests that peak water has already passed for this catchment, though the estimate is sensitive to how the debris cover is treated.

The survey will continue on the same schedule, and the raw stake readings are deposited with the national archive so that later workers can re-derive the balance series themselves.
